newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby Union-All Blacks eye Tri-Nations crown.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-All Blacks eye Tri-Nations crown.

text.p: The All Blacks made camp in New Zealand's wintry south this week, battle-weary but determined to beat the Australians at Dunedin on Saturday and take their second consecutive Tri-Nations crown.

Bruised and battered from their violent encounter with South Africa's Springboks last week, the New Zealanders are nevertheless secure in the knowledge that no team in the world at the moment has their measure.
The All Blacks remain unbeaten in seven tests this year.
They have conquered each of their Tri-Nations rivals twice -- last Saturday's 55-35 win the largest ever by an All Black side over South Africa.
Although seemingly invincible, coach John Hart said the New Zealand side would not fall victim to complacency.

"We've been focusing pretty clearly on the fact that this is an important day for us," Hart told Reuters. "We need to win the game to win the Tri-Nations, so I don't think we lack for motivation -- but nor do the Australians."
Australia could still lay claim to the coveted trophy by winning in Dunedin and then putting South Africa to the sword in the final game of the series in Pretoria on August 24.
Australia come off a 32-20 win against South Africa, but the signs look ominous for the Wallabies in Dunedin.
Coach Greg Smith knows his forwards must turn in a flawless performance if Australia is to have any chance of beating the All Blacks, and injury has dealt his scrum a devastating blow.
Inspirational Australian lock and skipper John Eales was this week ruled out of Saturday's clash after he damaged knee ligaments in training.

Flanker Matt Cockbain has also had to withdraw after a knock to the head, and a shoulder injury to number eight Daniel Manu means Australia will field a relatively inexperienced forward pack against arguably the best tight-five in the world.
"This has probably been the worst week I have ever experienced in my career as coach," Smith told reporters.

Flanker David Wilson will captain Australia in a test for the first time, while John Langford will make his test debut in Eales' locking position. Fili Finau comes off the reserves bench for Cockbain and veteran Troy Coker slots in at number eight.

Smith has delayed a decision on whether Andrew Blades will replace Andrew Heath as tighthead prop, and compounding his woes are flyhalf Tim Horan and dynamic fullback Matt Burke, both unavailable because of long-term injuries.

In stark contrast only one change has been made to the All Blacks' starting line-up, nimble-footed Glen Osborne replacing Tana Umaga on the left wing, although an injury scare has placed flyhalf Carlos Spencer in doubt.
Spencer strained a hamstring in training but it does not appear serious. Should he fail to recover in time, last year's star pivot Andrew Mehrtens will reclaim his test jersey.
The Wallabies have never won a test at Dunedin's Carisbrook, dubbed the "house of pain" for its cold climate and vocal student support of the home side.
The small South Island city promises to deliver both on Saturday, with a capacity 42,000 crowd and snow forecast.
Teams

New Zealand: 15-Christian Cullen, 14-Jeff Wilson, 13-Frank Bunce, 12-Alama Ieremia, 11-Glen Osborne, 10-Carlos Spencer or Andrew Mehrtens, 9-Justin Marshall, 8-Zinzan Brooke, 7-Josh Kronfeld, 6-Taine Randell, 5-Ian Jones, 4-Robin Brooke, 3-Olo Brown, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), 1-Craig Dowd.

Australia: 15-Stephen Larkham, 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Joe Roff, 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan, 8-Troy Coker, 7-David Wilson (captain), 6-Fili Finau, 5-John Langford, 4-Owen Finegan, 3-Andrew Blades or Andrew Heath, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.
